data.why: The app has no file upload component; every input (well name, KB, GL, geothermal gradients, MD/BHT runs) is typed directly into number fields in the browser, so there is no file to seed.

goals: register a vertical well's metadata (name, onshore/offshore region, kelly bushing level, ground level, mean annual surface/sea-floor temperature)
predict a pre-drill temperature-vs-depth profile from P90/P50/P10 geothermal gradients down to a target total depth
enter post-drill bottom-hole temperature (BHT) runs at multiple measured depths and correct them for drilling disturbance using the AAPG and Harrison et al. (1983) correction methods
compare predicted pre-drill temperature gradients against corrected post-drill gradients to assess how much drilling disturbed the temperature field
convert common well-engineering units (depth, temperature) between field and metric/absolute scales

review.summary: The tree captures what the tool is for (register a vertical well, forecast P90/P50/P10 temperatures, correct BHTs by AAPG and Harrison, compare, convert units), with phases at the right depth and numbers that check out against the screens. Before filing it needs a few fixes: two evidence citations don't match their screens, the offshore runs are framed as a 'second site', and the Depth Type control is described as changing the result when it only changes the plot axis.
